Backend: 7/7 new tests PASS — welcome/cert/invite emails fire-and-forget with real Resend sends (log line '[email/<tag>] Sent to <email> (resend id: <id>)' present within ~2s of API call), sender is 'no-reply@ithr.tech' (ithr.tech domain verified — no sandbox restriction), all three endpoints return in <1s and are non-blocking on Resend. Sample cert PDF endpoint still returns 200 + 25.8KB valid PDF (%PDF-1.7) with ITHR Teal #00A78B + Navy #16335E palette locked at template source. Frontend: /certificate/SAMPLE-ITHR-2026-001 (protected route) renders CertificateTutor widget (data-testid=cert-tutor) with 3 quick-ask buttons (data-testid^=cert-tutor-quick-0..2) and cert-tutor-input; clicking quick-ask streams a real 1205-char Aletheia response; typing 'What is agentic AI...' + Enter streams a follow-up (grew to 2371 chars total) via useTutorStream. Zero console errors. Regression: iter15+16+21 suites at 36/39 (92.3%) — 3 failures are pre-existing '.test'-TLD email-validator quirk in TestEnterpriseAdminCreateUser flagged as flaky for 5+ iterations in review request (NOT regressions from this iter).

minor.issue: Resend account is on the free tier (2 requests/sec cap). Under parallel load (pytest-xdist 2 workers, or a burst of ~5 signups within 1s) the third+ concurrent send raises RateLimitError. All raise points are swallowed via logger.exception so nothing blocks — but the affected recipient does NOT get an email. For a customer-facing prod deployment, either upgrade the Resend plan or add an internal token-bucket queue (e.g., aiolimiter) in email_service._fire keyed at ~1.8 req/s. Test suite works around this by throttling 0.8s between test invocations.

action_items: OPTIONAL P2: Add an internal 1.8 req/s token-bucket rate limiter in email_service._fire so bursts of signups/cert-issues don't silently drop welcome/cert emails on Resend's 2 req/s free-tier cap. Currently swallowed via logger.exception — no user-visible failure, but no email delivered either.

OPTIONAL P3 (pre-existing, iter-19 known): TestEnterpriseAdminCreateUser fixtures in test_iteration15.py generate test emails with '.test' TLD (e.g., cto+xxx@acme-xxx.test); pydantic EmailStr rejects '.test' as a reserved TLD → 422. Not a code bug; fix is to use '.example.com' or another IANA-reserved-but-Pydantic-accepted TLD in the test fixture. Not blocking anything.
critical_code_review_comments: email_service.py — Excellent shared wrapper. Single _fire() with logger.exception, common _wrap() shell, dedicated tags per email type ('welcome', 'cert', 'invite'). All three public functions return bool, never raise — matches the 'never block signup/cert-issuance on email' contract stated in the review request.

auth_router.register (L102-108) — asyncio.create_task properly wrapped in try/except → dispatched fire-and-forget; if wrap-import fails, register still returns 200. Elapsed <3s in tests confirms it never blocks. Good.

assessment_router._issue_certificate_if_new (L204-215) — Same fire-and-forget pattern via asyncio.create_task. Correct placement: only fires for NEW certs (existing certs return early at L184-186), so re-submitting a passing quiz for the same course doesn't spam the email. Good.
enterprise_router.create_invite (L117-131) — Fires invite email after invite doc insert; admin_user is fetched inside the try/except to avoid the create_task capturing a stale reference. Correct.

assessment_router PDF template (L384-462) — Palette lock is at the CSS-string source, not a runtime config. This is intentional and defensible (WeasyPrint parses a static string), but if the ITHR brand ever changes hex codes, both the CSS in email_service._wrap AND the PDF template in assessment_router must be updated in lockstep. Consider extracting to a shared brand_constants.py module. Non-blocking.

CertificateTutor.jsx — Cleanly reuses useTutorStream/TutorConversation from the tutor package; no code duplication with InlineTutor/AITutorPanel. quickAsks array keys use array index (L52 key={i}) — acceptable here since the array is static and length is fixed at 3.

Certificate.jsx L140 — CertificateTutor is rendered inside the '.max-w-4xl mx-auto' wrapper, which means the widget respects the cert-page grid. Section internal max-w-3xl is narrower than the credential card — good for readability.
